transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it's nice to meet you too. Um, what brings me in... I guess my head just feels really foggy lately. Like, I'm making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, and I'm a personal care aide, so you know, the notes are important. I was actually just at this one client's house, Mr. Henderson, he's such a sweet older guy, always wants to talk about his time in the Navy. He served on this huge aircraft carrier, I can't remember the name of it now, but he showed me pictures. Anyway, I keep forgetting what I was about to do when I'm there, which really isn't like me at all. I usually have my routine down pat. But yeah, the Navy pictures were really something, black and white, you know? But this foggy feeling, it's just throwing me off.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, exactly, it's just like I was saying with that foggy feeling. I sit down to do my client notes and I just can't focus, so I end up making these little mistakes. Or I'll walk into a room and completely forget what I was about to do. Which really isn't like me at all, you know? I usually have a mind like a steel trap. 

My buddy Dave always says I should've been an accountant because I'm usually so good with details. Dave actually just bought this old Chevy truck he's trying to fix up—completely rusted out, but he thinks he can get it running by summer. I told him he's out of his mind, parts for those things cost an absolute fortune now, especially the transmission. He had to drive three states over just to find a bumper. But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I just can't seem to keep my thoughts straight enough to get my work done right.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?

Well, it's funny you ask about sleep, because usually I'm out like a light by 10 PM. But lately... yeah, for several nights there I was only sleeping maybe three, four hours tops. And the weird thing is, I'd wake up feeling totally charged. Like, ready to go. I'd still make my morning coffee, but honestly, it was more just out of habit than actually needing it to wake up. 

I use this French press my sister got me for my birthday last year. She's really into all that artisanal coffee stuff, buys these beans from some little farm in Colombia. She actually went down there on vacation, said the mountains were unbelievable. Took a whole album of photos on her phone, mostly of these tiny little frogs she kept finding near her hotel. They were bright blue, if you can believe it. She said they're poisonous, but she got right up close anyway. Typical Sarah, always jumping into things without thinking. 

But yeah, I'd just sit there with my fancy coffee at 4 AM, not even tired, just... buzzing, I guess. It was strange.
During those days when you were sleeping only a few hours, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah, before this whole foggy, low feeling hit me, I did have a stretch where I felt... I don't know, almost too good? Like I was just on top of the world, feeling really powerful and capable of anything. But it was weird because one minute I'd be riding that high, and the next I'd just snap. I'd get so sharp with my wife over the dumbest little things, or I'd bite my coworkers' heads off if they didn't do something exactly right. 

My wife, she's usually so patient with me. We actually just celebrated our 15th anniversary. We went to this little Italian place downtown, the one with the red checkered tablecloths? They make this incredible lasagna, supposedly an old family recipe from Naples or somewhere. The owner came out and talked to us for like twenty minutes about his grandmother who started the place. He was wearing this wild tie, bright yellow with little green turtles all over it. I remember thinking, who wears a tie like that to run a restaurant? But the food was great. 

Anyway, yeah, I was feeling fantastic, just really on fire, but then I'd just get so irritable and snap at people. It was a weird mix.
During that energized stretch, were you more active than usual?

Yeah, I definitely was. I just couldn't sit still. It was like... if I stopped moving for even a second, all this grief and heavy stuff would just catch up to me, you know? So I just kept moving. I was making lists, running errands, calling people I haven't talked to in years, doing chores around the house. 

I actually decided to finally clean out the gutters, which I've been putting off forever. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he saw me up on the ladder and came over to give me advice. He's always doing that, thinks he's the neighborhood handyman just because he used to work in construction back in the eighties. He was telling me about this special type of sealant he uses on his roof, went on and on about the chemical composition of it. Honestly, I think he just gets lonely since his kids moved out. His daughter just had a baby, actually, a little girl. They named her something unique... Juniper, I think? Or maybe Willow. One of those nature names that are so popular right now. 

But yeah, I was just constantly finding things to do. If I wasn't doing something, I felt like I was going to explode.
During that energized stretch, did it cause serious problems at work or home?

Well, it definitely made things... messy. At work, I'm a personal care aide, so there's a lot of documentation for my clients. Lately, I've had to ask my coworkers to double-check my notes because I just keep missing things. Which reminds me, one of my clients, Mrs. Gable, she has this old grandfather clock in her hallway. Beautiful piece, dark mahogany, must be from the 1920s or something. It chimes every quarter hour, and she told me her late husband bought it at an antique auction in London. They used to travel everywhere before he passed. She showed me pictures of them in Egypt, riding camels right in front of the pyramids. The sky in the photos was this incredible, piercing blue... 

But anyway, yeah, at work I'm just not as reliable with the details right now. And at home, too. My wife has actually had to take over paying some of the bills and handling our schedule. She got this new planner, it's got these little stickers for different appointments. She's always been so organized, unlike me.
How many days in a row did that energized, sleeping-only-3-to-4-hours period last?

Well, let's see... it all started about two weeks ago. This whole shift really kicked in right after my uncle died. We were actually pretty close when I was a kid. He used to take me fishing out at this lake a couple hours from here. Lake... Oconee, I think? Yeah, Lake Oconee. We'd get up at the crack of dawn, pack these terrible bologna sandwiches on white bread with way too much mustard. He had this old aluminum boat that leaked just a little bit, so I always had to bail water out with a plastic Folgers coffee can while he handled the motor. The motor was this vintage Evinrude, smelled like gas and oil, but he swore by it. He said they didn't make them like that anymore. We caught a huge bass out there once, must have been five pounds. He had it mounted and put it in his den... 

But yeah, the not sleeping and all that energy, that started right after he passed, about two weeks ago.
Did that energized stretch last at least 4 days in a row?

Yeah, definitely. Like I said, this whole shift really started after my uncle died, which was about two weeks ago. And it's just been going ever since. Two weeks of just... zooming. It's funny, when my uncle died, they had this beautiful service for him. The floral arrangements were just incredible. There were these massive wreaths of white lilies and blue hydrangeas. My aunt, she insisted on hydrangeas because they were his mother's favorite flower. She grew them along the side of her house back in Ohio. The soil there must have been really acidic, because the flowers were always this deep, vibrant blue. I read once that you can change the color of hydrangeas by putting coffee grounds or pennies in the soil. I actually tried that in my own garden last spring, but the neighborhood stray cats kept digging it up. There's this one orange tabby that just won't leave my flowerbeds alone. He's got a nick in his left ear, looks like he's been in a few scraps... but yeah, it's been about two weeks straight of this.
During that energized stretch, did you feel more powerful or important than usual?

Well, yeah, I did. I honestly believed I could just quit waiting around and start my own Spanish-speaking senior-care agency right away. Like, I had it all figured out in my head and I just couldn't fail. It made so much sense. I mean, my grandmother spoke Spanish, and she used to make these amazing tamales every Christmas. The whole family would get together in her tiny kitchen. It was always so hot in there, the windows would steam up completely. She had this old cast-iron pot she used for the masa, must have weighed twenty pounds. My cousin Hector dropped it on his toe once when we were kids, broke it right in two places. He had to wear this clunky black boot for six weeks, which really messed up his soccer season. He was the star goalie for our high school team. They actually went to the state championships that year, played against a team from up north that had these blindingly bright neon green jerseys. You could see them from a mile away... but yeah, I just felt like I had all the answers and could start that agency without a hitch.
During that energized stretch, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah, I guess maybe a little? I don't know, it's hard to tell when you're just going and going. But you know who did talk a lot? My high school speech teacher, Mr. Gable. That guy could talk for hours about absolutely nothing. He had this weird habit of jingling the change in his pocket while he lectured, and it drove everyone crazy. It was always pennies and quarters, just clinking away. I tried saving quarters once in this big plastic Coke bottle bank I won at the county fair. The fair was great back then, they had this ride called the Zipper that just flipped you upside down over and over. I threw up a funnel cake on that ride when I was twelve. Powdered sugar everywhere. My mom was so mad she made me ride home in the bed of my dad's pickup truck. It was an old Chevy C10, light blue, with a cracked windshield on the passenger side from a stray golf ball... but yeah, I'm not really sure if I was talking more than usual or not.
During that energized period, did you have any hallucinations or beliefs that other people said were not true?

No, I didn't see anything that wasn't there, or think things that people said were crazy. I mean, my sister always tells me my ideas are crazy, but she's just like that. She's been super critical ever since we were kids. Like this one time, we were building a treehouse in the big oak out back, and she kept saying my knots weren't tied right. I learned how to tie knots in the Boy Scouts, actually. We had this scoutmaster, Mr. Henderson, who used to take us camping up near the lake. The mosquitoes there were just huge, like the size of small birds. I got bit so many times on my ankles that summer I had to wear these thick wool socks even though it was ninety degrees out. Wool socks are the worst when it's hot, they make your feet sweat so much and then they smell like wet dog. We had a dog, a golden retriever named Buster, who loved swimming in that lake... but no, I didn't have anything like what you're asking about.
Before your uncle died, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt this unusually energized and needed much less sleep?

No, I don't think so. I mean, not that I can remember before he passed. His funeral was really hard, actually. We had it at this little church off Route 9, the one with the white steeple that needs painting. The paint was peeling off in these big strips, looked like sunburned skin. I always peel my sunburns, even though you're not supposed to. I got a terrible burn in Florida back in '98. We drove all the way down there in a Honda Civic, four of us crammed in. The AC broke somewhere in Georgia, and we had to roll the windows down, which just blew all this hot, humid air in our faces. My buddy Dave was in the backseat, and he kept complaining about his knees being cramped. He's like six-foot-three, played basketball for a community college in Ohio. They actually made it to some regional tournament, but he sprained his ankle right before the first game. He was so bummed out, he just sat on the bench eating those little bags of pretzels they sell at the concession stand... but yeah, before my uncle, I don't remember ever feeling that revved up or skipping sleep like that.
Did this burst of energy and confidence feel clearly unlike the kind of reaction you would normally have after a loss?

I don't know, honestly. I mean, everybody handles grief differently, right? When my aunt passed, my cousin cried for like three weeks straight. She couldn't even go to work. She worked at this bakery downtown, the one that makes those amazing blueberry scones. I used to go there every Tuesday morning before my shift. I'm a personal care aide, so I have to be up pretty early to help my clients get out of bed and dressed. One of my guys, Mr. Higgins, he's got this old basset hound that just howls every time the toaster pops. It's the funniest thing. The dog is practically deaf, but he knows the exact sound of that toaster. He loves toast with a little bit of butter on it. Real butter, not the margarine stuff. Margarine is basically just oil and water anyway, I saw a documentary about how they make it in these massive vats... but yeah, I couldn't really tell you if the way I reacted was normal or not.
During those two weeks, did your wife or coworkers say you seemed noticeably different from your usual self?

I don't really remember my wife or the guys at work saying anything about me acting different. My wife was pretty distracted anyway because we were dealing with this leak in the downstairs bathroom. The pipe under the sink kept dripping, just this constant tap-tap-tap all day. It really gets under your skin. We ended up having to call a plumber, this guy named Mike who drives a bright neon green van. You literally can't miss it. He told me he painted it green because his daughter's favorite color is emerald. She's in a high school marching band, plays the trombone, I think. I tried to play the trumpet back in middle school, but I could never get my lips to do the right thing on the mouthpiece. It just sounded like a dying elephant every time I blew into it. Our band teacher, Mr. Davies, had the worst comb-over I've ever seen in my life, he used to sweat so much during the concerts... but no, I don't think anyone told me I was acting out of the ordinary.
During that energized period, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive?

No, I don't think I did anything really risky. I mean, I'm usually a pretty careful guy. Like, I always check the tire pressure on my car before a long trip. You know, you can get better gas mileage if your tires are inflated right. I read this article once that said most people are driving around on under-inflated tires and wasting all this money on gas. Gas prices are just crazy right now, anyway. I remember when I first started driving, I could fill up my tank for like fifteen bucks. It was a '89 Ford Escort, manual transmission. I loved that car, but the clutch went out on me when I was stuck in traffic on the George Washington Bridge. That was a nightmare. Cars were honking, people were yelling, and I'm just sitting there sweating buckets trying to get it into gear. The tow truck took forever to get there because of the traffic, and the driver was this huge guy who looked like a professional wrestler... but yeah, I don't remember doing anything wild or impulsive.
During that energized period, did your wife notice that you seemed unusually upbeat or irritable compared with your normal self?

Well, I guess before I crashed and started feeling this low, there was a stretch where I felt... I don't know, almost too good? Like really powerful, you know? But then the next minute I'd get real sharp with my wife over nothing, or snap at the guys at work. My wife actually said I was acting like a completely different person when we were trying to pick out a new rug for the living room. We went to this huge warehouse store, the kind where you have to have a membership card just to get in the door. I always lose those cards. I must have had them print me like five replacements in the last year. The lady at the customer service desk was giving me this look, you know, like I was the biggest idiot she'd ever seen. She had these bright pink acrylic nails with little rhinestones on them. I don't know how people type with nails like that, it seems like they'd get caught in the keyboard... but anyway, yeah, I'd feel on top of the world and then just snap at her out of nowhere.
During that energized time, were you getting a lot more done than usual?

Oh, definitely. I was pushing hard on all these plans at once, like it was nothing. I was sorting out memorial details, getting car repairs done, looking into CNA classes so I could move up at work, and coming up with all these new business ideas. I was calling up my relatives and coworkers way more than I normally would, too. I actually called my cousin Greg like three times in one day about this idea I had for a mobile dog grooming business. Greg has this golden retriever named Buster who sheds like crazy. I mean, there's just hair everywhere in his house. You sit on his couch and you stand up looking like you're wearing a fur coat. He tried buying one of those robot vacuums to keep up with it, but Buster hates the thing. He barks at it whenever it comes out of its little charging dock. It's one of those off-brand ones, not a real Roomba, so it always gets stuck under the coffee table anyway and just beeps until you rescue it... but yeah, I was just juggling a million things at once.
During that energized time, were you working toward specific goals much more than usual?

I mean, not really anything besides what I just told you about the CNA classes and the business stuff. I don't think I had like, a big master plan or anything. It's funny you mention goals, though, because my buddy Dave at the clinic—he's another aide there—he has this massive goal to visit every national park in the country before he turns fifty. He just took his RV out to Yellowstone last month. He was telling me all about how terrible the gas mileage is on those things. It's like driving a brick down the highway. Plus, he said the campsites are always completely booked up months in advance now. People just sit at their computers waiting for the reservations to open and boom, they're gone in two seconds. I could never plan a vacation like that. I like to just get in the car and see where the road takes me, you know? Like this one time I just drove up the coast for no reason and ended up at this diner that had the best cherry pie I've ever eaten... but yeah, I don't think I had any other big goals going on.
During that energized period, did you get into any serious arguments or problems at work because of how irritable or intense you were?

No, not really. I mean, I snapped at people, like I said, but nobody wrote me up or anything. I've been at that clinic for a while, so people kind of know me. Though, honestly, management there is so disorganized they probably wouldn't notice unless someone actually threw a punch. The HR lady, Brenda, she's always on leave. I swear she's taken three maternity leaves in the last four years. She brought the newest baby into the breakroom a few weeks ago, and it had this little knit hat with bear ears on it. Someone made it for her off Etsy, I think. Etsy's crazy, right? You can buy anything on there. My wife bought these custom wooden coasters with our initials burned into them, but they warp if you put a hot mug on them, which completely defeats the purpose of a coaster if you ask me. You're supposed to protect the table, not worry about ruining the coaster... but no, no big blowups at work or anything like that.
During that energized stretch, did other people clearly notice that you were not acting like your usual self?

I don't think anyone really said anything to me about it. Maybe they noticed, but people usually keep to themselves, you know? Especially my neighbor, Tom. He's one of those guys who will just give you a little nod if you're both out getting the mail, but he never actually stops to talk. He's always out there working on his lawn, though. He's got this riding mower that looks like a small tractor, and he's out there every Saturday morning at exactly 8:00 AM. It's so loud it wakes up my wife, and she gets so mad because Saturday is her only day to sleep in. She works at the grocery store down the street, the one that just got bought out by that big chain. They completely rearranged the aisles, and now she says customers are constantly yelling at her because they can't find the bread. They moved it all the way to the back corner next to the frozen foods, which makes absolutely no sense. Why would you put bread next to the freezers? It's just going to get cold and stale... but yeah, nobody really pointed out that I was acting differently or anything.

patient.answer:
Yeah, before this whole foggy, low feeling hit me, I did have a stretch where I felt... I don't know, almost too good? Like I was just on top of the world, feeling really powerful and capable of anything. But it was weird because one minute I'd be riding that high, and the next I'd just snap. I'd get so sharp with my wife over the dumbest little things, or I'd bite my coworkers' heads off if they didn't do something exactly right. 

My wife, she's usually so patient with me. We actually just celebrated our 15th anniversary. We went to this little Italian place downtown, the one with the red checkered tablecloths? They make this incredible lasagna, supposedly an old family recipe from Naples or somewhere. The owner came out and talked to us for like twenty minutes about his grandmother who started the place. He was wearing this wild tie, bright yellow with little green turtles all over it. I remember thinking, who wears a tie like that to run a restaurant? But the food was great.
